questions.text: Is climate action the core purpose or goal of the policy?
questions.answer: The policy under review, the North Sydney Council Environmental Sustainability Strategy 2030, clearly identifies climate action as a core purpose. The policy outlines a comprehensive plan to address climate change and environmental sustainability, with specific actions, targets, and performance measures. The policy's focus on climate action is evident in its commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, increasing renewable energy capacity, and advocating for higher resource use standards. The policy also aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, further emphasizing its commitment to environmental sustainability. The policy's action plan includes specific actions related to carbon footprint, engagement in sustainability, and urban ecology, all of which contribute to climate action. Therefore, it is clear that climate action is a core purpose of the policy.

questions.text: Does the document explicitly explain the need for action on climate change?
questions.answer: The documents clearly articulate the need for action on climate change. The North Sydney Council has been actively reducing greenhouse gas emissions for years to lessen its energy consumption and impact on climate change. The Council set its first greenhouse gas reduction targets in 2002 as part of the International Council for Local Environmental Initiatives (ICLEI) Cities for Climate Protection (CCP) program. The Council's 2030 targets and actions are a response to the climate crisis and provide a roadmap to accelerate towards a carbon-neutral future. The Council's actions include conducting energy audits at Council facilities, adopting and implementing Sustainable Building Standards, increasing Council's renewable energy capacity, and purchasing 100% renewable electricity. The Council also plans to advocate for the protection/increase of tree canopy cover across all local and state government projects and develop an Urban Forest Incentives program.

questions.text: Does the document explicitly call for rapid and urgent action on climate change?
questions.answer: The documents from the North Sydney Council clearly call for urgent action on climate change. The council declared a climate emergency on 22 July 2019, noting the latest report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the increasing carbon emissions. This declaration signifies the council's recognition of the urgent need for immediate action at all levels of government. The council has set ambitious targets for 2030, including meeting 100% of the council’s electricity needs from renewable energy sources, achieving 100% carbon neutrality for council operations, and reducing community emissions by 25% from 1996 levels. The council has also developed an action plan to achieve these targets, indicating a commitment to rapid action. However, it is important to note that while the council has declared a climate emergency and set ambitious targets, the success of these actions will depend on their effective implementation and the cooperation of the community and other levels of government.

The North Sydney Council's Environmental Sustainability Strategy 2030 outlines a detailed action plan with clear responsibilities, timeframes, and performance measures. For instance, the plan includes actions such as conducting and implementing findings of energy audits at Council facilities every four years, adopting and implementing the Sustainable Building Standards for Council-owned facilities to reduce their energy-related carbon footprint, and increasing Council's renewable energy capacity. questions.text: Does the document provide well-sourced evidence to justify its climate targets and actions?
questions.answer: The documents provide a well-sourced evidence base to justify its climate targets and actions. The North Sydney Council has engaged Energetics, a consultancy, to review its progress against targets, develop new management plans for 2015 - 2020, assess how to achieve the 2020 targets and recommend new targets for 2030. The process involved a comprehensive review of local, state, federal and international strategies and applied them to the North Sydney context. The Council also conducted energy audits at its facilities and developed a Sustainable Building Standards for Council owned facilities to reduce their energy related carbon footprint. The Council's progress against targets was also outlined, with a 49% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from the 1996 baseline level and 35% savings in potable water consumption from the 2001/02 baseline level. The Council also has an environmental levy to fund sustainability initiatives.
